q-81614.name: Question 1
q-81614.worked_solution:
First, we can factor out the conjunction with $Q,$ as follows:

$$
(P∧Q)∨(R∧Q)≡(P∨R)∧Q
$$

Then, we can write

$$
(P∨R)∧Q≡Q∧(P∨R).
$$

q-81614.html:
Question 1
?

Which statement is equivalent to (P∧Q)∨(R∧Q)?

a
(P∨Q)∨R
b
(P∧R)∧Q
c
Q∨(P∨R)
d
Q∧(P∨R)
e
(P∨Q)∧R
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we can factor out the conjunction with Q, as follows:

(P∧Q)∨(R∧Q)≡(P∨R)∧Q

Then, we can write (P∨R)∧Q≡Q∧(P∨R).

q-128628.name: Question 2
q-128628.worked_solution:
We distribute the disjunction over the conjunction, as follows:

$$
(¬X∧¬Y)∨Z≡(¬X∨Z)∧(¬Y∨Z)
$$

q-128629.html:
Question 3
?

Which statement is equivalent to A∨(¬B∧C)?

a
(A∨¬B)∧(¬B∨C)
b
(A∨¬B)∧(A∨C)
c
(A∨¬B)∧C
d
(A∨¬B)∨(A∨C)
e
(A∧¬B)∨(A∧C)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We distribute the disjunction over the conjunction, as follows: A∨(¬B∧C)≡(A∨¬B)∧(A∨C)

q-128637.name: Question 4
q-128637.worked_solution:
We distribute the conjunction over the disjunction, as follows:

$$
A∧(¬Y∨C)≡(A∧¬Y)∨(A∧C)
$$

Now, since $A∧¬Y≡¬Y∧A$ and $A∧C≡C∧A,$ we can write

$$
(A∧¬Y)∨(A∧C)≡(¬Y∧A)∨(C∧A).
$$

q-128637.html:
Question 4
?

Which statement is equivalent to A∧(¬Y∨C)?

a
(¬Y∧A)∧(C∧A)
b
A∨(¬Y∧C)
c
(¬Y∧A)∨(C∧A)
d
(C∧¬Y)∨(C∧A)
e
C∧(A∨¬Y)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We distribute the conjunction over the disjunction, as follows:

A∧(¬Y∨C)≡(A∧¬Y)∨(A∧C)

Now, since A∧¬Y≡¬Y∧A and A∧C≡C∧A, we can write

(A∧¬Y)∨(A∧C)≡(¬Y∧A)∨(C∧A).

q-128649.name: Question 5
q-128649.worked_solution:
We can factor out the disjunction with $¬R,$ as follows:

$$
(P∨¬R)∧(Q∨¬R)≡(P∧Q)∨¬R
$$

Question 5
?

Which statement is equivalent to (P∨¬R)∧(Q∨¬R)?

a
¬R∧(P∧Q)
b
(P∨Q)∧¬R
c
(P∧Q)∨¬R
d
¬R∨(P∨Q)
e
(P∧¬R)∨Q
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We can factor out the disjunction with ¬R, as follows:

(P∨¬R)∧(Q∨¬R)≡(P∧Q)∨¬R
